text.p: Steffi Graf's youth and adult life has been dominated by her father Peter.

In the past his behaviour has upset his daughter's form but during the recent tax scandal which will reach a climax on Friday with a German court verdict, Graf has shown a remarkable ability to switch off from the problems and win matches.
Here is a chronology of the ups-and-downs of their lives:
June 14 1969 -- Steffi Graf born in Bruehl, Germany.
1973 - Peter first recognises Steffi's talent when she starts hitting a ball against a wall at home.
1977 - Graf wins a children's tournament in Munich. Peter gives up his job as a second-hand car salesman to concentrate on training and marketing of Steffi. Starts up tennis centre.
1983 - After winning major titles in youth tennis during 1981 and 1982, Graf makes name for herself by reaching second round at French Open, one of the youngest players to do so.
1985 - The year of the first big successes. Steffi reaches semifinals of U.S. Open and moves into top 10 for first time.

1986 - Graf becomes force on circuit, winning eight tournaments. Boris Becker's Wimbledon triumph (1985) has set off a tennis boom in Germany. Peter knows there is big money to be made with sponsors. Graf voted German sportswoman of year for first time. Earnings from sponsorship deals already estimated to be around $1.3 million. Peter Graf decides against move to tax haven of Monaco.
1987 - Graf wins first grand slam title at Roland Garros. Estimated to earn more than $3.6 million in sponsorship deals during the year before prize money taken into account.
1988 - Graf dominates game, winning all four grand slams. Makes estimated $6 million in sponsorship deals.

1990 - Graf family hit by scandal in the German papers about her father (52) and nude model Nicole Meissner (22). Steffi admits she is struggling to concentrate on game, threatens to leave Germany for U.S. and surprisingly loses in the final of French Open. Steffi says she will never stop hating the journalists. Paternity suits follows.

1991 - Peter Graf involved in exchange of blows in players' box at French Open while Steffi is losing semifinal. Meissner's law suit against Peter fails when blood tests showed he is not father of her baby. Graf loses number one spot -- because of the sex scandal, Peter says. German tax authorities start to probe Graf's financial dealings.
1993 - Rival Monica Seles ruled out of the game for several seasons after being stabbed by deranged Graf fan at Hamburg Open. Graf says the incident puts her under extra pressure.
1994 - Tax authorities fear that not all Graf's earnings are being declared. Graf wins Australian Open.
March 1995 - Authorities ask Graf advisor Joachim Eckardt for details of undeclared earnings by April 21. None are given.
April 26 1995 - Official start of tax investigations.
May 23 1995 - Tax authorities search Graf homes in Germany.
June 10 1995 - Graf wins French Open
July 8 1995 - Graf wins Wimbledon
July 12 1995 - German media break news of May tax raids, the start of intense media coverage during the scandal.
August 2 1995 - Peter arrested, refused bail and jailed while investigation continues. Receives hospital treatment.
September 9 1995 - Graf wins U.S. Open but leaves press conference in tears after being asked about father.
September 26 1995 - Eckardt also arrested and put in jail. In the next few months courts refuse several times to release two men on bail saying they fear they may leave the country.
October 1995 - German car firm Opel end 10-year sponsorship deal with Graf, one of longest in German sport.
April 17 1996 - Graf and Eckardt, still in prison, accused of avoiding around $11.5 million in tax.
June 8 1996 - Graf wins fifth French Open title.
July 6 1996 - Graf wins seventh Wimbledon singles title.
September 5 1996 - Court case starts in Mannheim.
September 8 1996 - Graf wins fifth U.S. Open title
November 15 1996 - Peter Graf released from jail after paying $3.3 million in bail after 15 months in custody. Steffi, playing in U.S., says she can't wait to get home to see him.
January 14 1997 - German prosecutors ask court to jail Graf for six years and nine months.
January 15 1997 - Women's tour WTA says it probing allegations Graf took appearance money for tournaments, which is banned.
January 19 1997 - Graf campaign for fifth Australian Open title ends in surprise fourth round defeat to South Africa's Amanda Coetzer.
